# WHAT IS THIS FILE?
# robots.txt is a plain-text file with a standardized format that "well
# behaved" web crawlers/bots (Googlebot, Bingbot, etc.) check BEFORE they
# start crawling a site, to learn which parts of the site they're allowed
# to visit and index. It lives at a fixed, predictable URL —
# https://<your-domain>/robots.txt — which is why it must sit directly in
# Rails' public/ directory (the same directory the web server serves
# static files from with no Ruby code involved) rather than being
# generated by a Rails controller/view.
#
# WHY IS IT EMPTY OF ACTUAL RULES RIGHT NOW?
# This file currently contains no `User-agent:`/`Allow:`/`Disallow:`
# directives at all — just this documentation comment. An empty/rule-less
# robots.txt is interpreted by crawlers as "no restrictions specified,"
# meaning they'll assume they're free to crawl the entire site by default.
# If StorageFinder later wants to block crawlers from certain paths (e.g.
# admin pages, search results with infinite parameter combinations), rules
# would need to be added here, such as:
#   User-agent: *
#   Disallow: /admin
#
# HOW COMMENTS WORK IN THIS FILE:
# robots.txt uses `#` to start a comment — everything from a `#` to the end
# of that line is ignored by crawlers and is purely for human readers (this
# is the standard comment syntax across Ruby, YAML, and shell scripts too,
# which is why this same style guide uses `#` here).
#
# This single line (below) is the only content that shipped with this file
# by default: a pointer to the official specification/documentation for
# anyone who wants to read the full robots.txt syntax and add real rules.
# See https://www.robotstxt.org/robotstxt.html for documentation on how to use the robots.txt file
